hook: A guitar string, a car bouncing on its springs after a pothole, a child on a swing and the quartz crystal timing your phone all do the same thing: they go back and forth, over and over, about a middle position. Physics has one model that describes all of them, and it starts with a single rule about the force.

prereq.q: A spring with k = 50 N/m is stretched 0.10 m. How large is the force it exerts?
prereq.why: Hooke's law: |F| = kΔx = (50 N/m)(0.10 m) = 5.0 N.

prereq.q: An object has zero net force on it. What must be true?
prereq.why: Zero net force means zero acceleration, so the velocity does not change. The object can be moving.

prereq.q: A 2.0 kg object has a net force of 6.0 N on it. What is its acceleration?

figure.caption: The spring force on the cart always points back toward equilibrium and is proportional to the displacement.

chain.cause: An object is displaced from its equilibrium position
chain.effect: a restoring force pulls it back toward equilibrium

chain.cause: The restoring force is proportional to the displacement and opposite to it (F = −kx)
chain.effect: the acceleration is largest at the ends and zero at equilibrium

chain.cause: The object reaches equilibrium moving fast
chain.effect: it overshoots, because zero force does not stop it

chain.cause: On the other side the restoring force reverses
chain.effect: the object slows, stops at the same distance A, and comes back: simple harmonic motion

ideas: Periodic motion repeats in equal time intervals. Simple harmonic motion (SHM) is the special case caused by a restoring force proportional to the displacement: F = −kx.
The equilibrium position is where the net force is zero. The object moves fastest there, so zero force does not mean zero velocity.
The amplitude A is the largest displacement from equilibrium: half the distance from one turning point to the other.
A simple pendulum at small angles is close to SHM: along its arc the restoring force is about mg·θ, proportional to the angle (in radians).

misconception.wrong: At the turning points the object is at rest, so the force on it is zero; at the middle it is moving fastest, so the force there is largest.
misconception.right: It is the other way round. The force depends on the displacement, not on the speed: it is largest at the turning points (where the object is momentarily at rest) and zero at equilibrium (where it moves fastest).

summary: Simple harmonic motion is periodic motion driven by a restoring force proportional to the displacement from equilibrium and opposite to it (F = −kx); the force and acceleration are zero at equilibrium and largest at the amplitude, and a pendulum at small angles is a close match.
